businessType: Mid-size consulting firm, ~140 staff, delivering operations and technology advisory across three practice areas (Operations, Data/Analytics, Change Management) to two broad client segments: large-enterprise accounts and mid-market accounts. Founded 2008.
stage: $15.0M revenue, roughly flat YoY (was $14.8M prior year). Gross margin 42%. EBITDA declined from $2.4M (16%) two years ago to $1.6M (11%) last year to a run-rate ~$1.2M (8%) this year. Headcount roughly flat. Firm-wide billable utilization reported at a blended 68%.
ownerGoal: Restore EBITDA margin to 14-16% within 12-18 months without large layoffs, while protecting the firm's reputation and senior consultant retention.
ownerConstraints: People constraint: senior consultants are the firm's product; aggressive layoffs would damage delivery quality and reputation and are off the table for the managing partners.
Reputation constraint: firm competes on relationships and referrals; cannot be seen cutting corners or repricing existing clients abruptly.
Capital constraint: privately held, funds growth from operating cash; limited appetite for a big external strategy spend.
Governance constraint: managing-partner committee has already circulated an internal memo attributing the margin decline to 'market softness'; reversing that publicly requires evidence.
Time constraint: partners want a remediation plan agreed within 6 weeks ahead of next-year resourcing decisions.
immediateConcern: Managing partner framing: 'Our margins are down because the market has softened - clients are delaying projects and squeezing fees across the board, and everyone in our space is feeling it. Revenue held flat only because we fought hard. This is a demand-environment problem, not an us problem. We want a plan to ride out the soft market and protect the team - not an internal witch hunt. The committee has already concluded it is market softness.'
availableData: Revenue flat ($14.8M -> $15.0M); EBITDA margin down 16% -> 11% -> 8% over three years while revenue held flat.

Blended billable utilization 68% this year, reported only firm-wide; prior-year blended utilization was 74%. Utilization has NOT been broken out by practice area, by grade (partner/manager/consultant/analyst), or by client segment.
Realization rate (billed vs standard rate) reported blended at ~91%; not broken out by client or engagement type.

Client-segment revenue mix shifted: mid-market revenue grew from ~25% to ~40% of total over two years; large-enterprise revenue shrank correspondingly. Per-segment delivery cost and margin have never been computed.
Bench/non-billable time rose; an internal note attributes it to 'fewer projects,' but no analysis links specific idle staff to specific lost or delayed engagements.
Win-rate and proposal-volume data exist in the CRM but have not been pulled; partners cite a 'general sense' that clients are delaying.
Two large-enterprise anchor accounts reduced spend last year; whether they churned, paused, or were displaced by a competitor was not investigated.
unavailableData: Utilization and realization split by practice area, grade, and client segment.
Per-client-segment profitability (mid-market vs large-enterprise gross margin after fully-loaded delivery cost).
Win-rate and proposal-volume trend from the CRM to test whether demand actually fell or whether the firm is losing competitive bids.
Engagement-level margin analysis to see whether fixed-fee projects are overrunning budgeted hours.
External market benchmark confirming that comparable firms are seeing the same fee/utilization pressure.
timeHorizon: 12-18 months to restore margin; remediation plan due in 6 weeks
